original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: For the donor-set target κ > 0.1, certify aggregate moment floors under current bit and complex coverage/rank caps, exact unpaid/depth thresholds, and the selected bit word's local-only cost under profile-preserving coverage changes.
scope_change_reason: The user raised the target from the repository planning target κ > 0.01 to κ > 0.1. The initial exact target-level screen found that u=2 just opens the ideal bit floor. A bounded follow-up applies the pinned selected bit histogram to that changed law, then prices the local histogram alone to determine whether any coverage-only change at the same call width can cross the target.
bottleneck_link: The aggregate rank-cap floor tests ideal high-rank repacking. The pinned selected bit local histogram alone has moment 1.195680 at a=1/9, so profile-preserving coverage changes at the same families-per-call cannot reach the target even after every other charge is deleted.
stop_rule: Stop this aggregate screen once the strict a=1/9 obstruction and exact unpaid/rank boundaries are certified. Do not expand to another search unless one complete dirty endpoint or row-coefficient invoice can realize a passing boundary with margin.
evidence: Exact rational ninth-power comparisons prove that with one unpaid coordinate the centre-free minimum moment is >1 at bit R=53 and complex R=51. At the current caps, the ideal aggregate floor first drops below one at bit u=2 and complex u=3 centre-free / u=4 with centre retained. The pinned paired-plane identity-fit candidate (u=2,c=112) has floor approximately 1.02818 at a=1/9 and also needs u=4 to pass this aggregate budget. With one unpaid coordinate, deleting centre requires R=56 (bit) and R=65 (complex), first allowed by the halving guard at depths 6 and 6. This is a necessary-budget screen only; no supplier, replacement coverage identity, or higher-depth row invoice is constructed. The pinned selected bit histogram alone has exact outward-rational moment 1.195680 at a=1/9 after deleting the centre and all idle children. Thus no profile-preserving coverage-only change at the same w=296/3 can pass. At u=2 and R=53 the full relaxed profile gives 1.365696 with the centre and 1.355508 without it. Fractionally repacking all 5,129 local rank mass at one uniform rank first passes at ranks 53 with the centre (rank52 gives 1.001209) and 48 centre-free (rank47 gives 1.000411). These are fixed-profile screens only.
